key_insight: Thermally induced stresses in thin-film NiTi bilayers enable controlled self-folding of microscale origami architectures for biomedical implants.
engineering_relevance: Compact, autonomously folding structures could support minimally invasive neurovascular implant delivery and tailored deployment.
method: Model thermal-mismatch bending in NiTi–molybdenum and NiTi–SS316L bilayer hinges using finite elements.
Optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape for prescribed mountain and valley folds.
Integrate optimized hinges into a waterbomb origami unit cell to assess coordinated folding.
evidence_signal: Finite element simulations identify a hinge geometry enabling approximately 50% smaller unit-cell dimensions than previously reported designs and demonstrate coordinated folding in a complete waterbomb unit cell.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based feasibility; experimental validation and safe thermal actuation under physiological conditions remain unestablished.
paper_title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
